name: Kung Po Prawns
assumptions: Recipe serves 4 based on 400g prawns (standard 100g per serving for a main dish with rice), 450g water chestnuts, and 85g peanuts as bulk ingredients
Total active preparation and cooking time estimated at 25 minutes: 10 min marinating (passive), ~5 min frying prawns, ~5 min stir-frying aromatics and peanuts, ~5 min simmering with sauce
'to taste' ginger conservatively classified as present but quantity ambiguous
Soy sauce and cornflour (cornstarch) assumed standard types; soy sauce introduces wheat unless certified gluten-free (hence null for Gluten-free)
Peanuts introduce peanut allergen; chillies assumed to be standard red chillies without tree nut cross-contact
No milk, eggs, fish (distinct from shellfish/prawns), sesame, or tree nuts explicitly present
Pescatarian true as only seafood (prawns) is the animal product; vegetarian/vegan false due to prawns
Dairy-free true as no dairy ingredients listed
Water chestnuts, tomato puree, sugars, oil, garlic all compatible with listed diets where true
Instructions reference 'remaining soy sauce' but total quantified as 2 tbsp across both uses per provided data
instructions:
Mix the cornflour and 1 tbsp soy sauce, toss in the prawns and set aside for 10 mins. Stir the vinegar, remaining soy sauce, tomato purée, sugar and 2 tbsp water together to make a sauce.

When you’re ready to cook, heat a large frying pan or wok until very hot, then add 1 tbsp oil. Fry the prawns until they are golden in places and have opened out– then tip them out of the pan.

Heat the remaining oil and add the peanuts, chillies and water chestnuts. Stir-fry for 2 mins or until the peanuts start to colour, then add the ginger and garlic and fry for 1 more min. Tip in the prawns and sauce and simmer for 2 mins until thickened slightly. Serve with rice.
